A.claim: The ordering of Z enters a proof of Beal at exactly one point: positivity forbids cancellation, giving A^x < C^z, B^y < C^z and C^z <= 2 max(A^x,B^y). Hence with A^x <= B^y, C is pinned to within a factor 2^(1/z) <= 1.26 of B^(y/z). Over Z[i] this fails completely - the Helenius identity collapses norm 125 summands to a norm 16 sum.

B.claim: Height-gap hypothesis H: with A^x dominant and A<C, A^x <= (C-1)^z, which would give B^y >= z(C-1)^(z-1), an effective lower bound on B in terms of C.
